claims.claim: English noun attested by mid-14th century in a negative plotting/unlawful-design sense
Derived through Anglo-French/Old French conspiracie from Latin conspiratio/conspirationem
Latin ancestor is glossed with agreement/union/unanimity as well as the ancestry of later plotting senses
Neutral/good English verbal sense of conspire ('contribute jointly to a result') is dated by Etymonline to the 1530s
The phrase conspiracy theory existed before its modern strongly pejorative usage; Etymonline notes 19th-century non-pejorative use and a mid-20th-century development

caution: These records seed the investigation. They are claims from secondary lexical sources, not independently verified primary attestations.
